title: InvarOS Qualification Attestation v1
description: An independent verifier's derived conclusion about a Qualification Transcript. Only this artifact carries a status, and only a verifier sharing no code with the subject may sign it. See invaros/ADR-002 and founder decision QE-D2.

subject_build_digest.description: Re-checked by the verifier against a release manifest, never trusted from the transcript. Absent from every manifest yields status indeterminate.

criteria_manifest_digest.description: The verifier's own independently obtained copy. Taking this from the transcript would defeat the independence the split exists to create.

specification_digest.description: Carried through from the transcript, including a declared absence. NORMATIVE, and not expressible in schema: when this is a declared absence the attestation MUST NOT list specification_digest in validity.binds_to, because an artifact cannot bind to an identity it does not have. Enforced by test in the verifier repository, in the manner of the transcript's manifest_digest requirement.

declaredAbsence.description: A stated absence, drawn from a closed vocabulary. Identical to the transcript's definition and deliberately so: the two artifacts must agree on how an absence is spelled, or a consumer comparing them would read a difference where there is none.

digestOrDeclaredAbsence.description: Either a real digest of real bytes, or an explicit stated absence. NEVER a digest of something else -- see QE1-F1.

status.description: qualified requires an empty units_not_executed: a run that passed every case it executed but skipped a unit is incomplete, never qualified. indeterminate covers verifier-side resolution failure and is distinct from not-qualified, which is a substantive result. There is deliberately no partial status (QE-D7).

units_not_executed.description: Verifier-derived, not adopted from the subject's declaration. A disagreement with the transcript is reported in findings.

reasonCode.description: Closed vocabulary, per QE-D7. Here the value is verifier-derived and is what a consumer binds to.

finding.description: A reportable disagreement between what the subject declared and what the verifier derived, in the same class as a criteria-digest mismatch.

kind.description: environment-identity-absent was added by WP-02.0 (QE-D17). The transcript schema permits a transcript that names no architecture, so that no artifact valid before the amendment became invalid after it; this finding kind is where the verifier says so. Without it a transcript that stated nothing about its environment and one that stated environment-equivalence would be indistinguishable in the attestation, and absence would stop carrying information.

claim.description: The semantic domain of the claim travels with the claim (architecture P4, goal G3). An attestation without a supported domain cannot be emitted. This is the schematized form of the discipline SESSION_LEVEL2_QUALIFICATION.md already practises in prose.

validity.description: Digest-bound, never time-bounded (QE-D10). An attestation is voided by a change to a bound identity, not by elapsed time. not_valid_after, advisory expiry, and any other clock-dependent validity field are prohibited in v1; additionalProperties false is what makes that prohibition structural. This preserves offline and air-gapped verification without a freshness or trusted-clock dependency.

voided_by.const: any change to a bound identity — never elapsed time

signature.description: ES256, per founder decision QE-D15. The verifier's key is a distinct holder from the subject's: compromise of one does not forge the other's artifact.
